title: Josephine Baker and Valaida Snow
summary: He recalls Josephine Baker's start as a Boston chorus girl, Russell Smith's gift of a car, and hanging around with her and Valaida Snow.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: I was just trying to get into some things of that era, some of the great performers. Can you think of any others that you knew? Did you know Josephine Baker?
Oh, my goodness, how could I forget her? Josephine Baker was in Boston. She was a Boston girl. Her and -- what's the guy that played trumpet?
Valaida Snow.

Valaida Snow. Her and Val da were on the same show together. And Josephine, she was doing a chorus girl, and she got out of step and lost that. And she started dancing. And the band kept on playing til she got off, and the man said, you keep that in. And Josephine Baker -- that was up in Boston.
Russell Smith was a trumpet player.
Uh-huh, Russell Smith. There were a few brothers --
Yeah, Joe Smith and John Smith.
Is that so?
Yeah.
A lot of good trumpet players.
All trumpet players. And Josephine --
Why do you mention Russell Smith in conjunction with --
Because Russell gave Josephine a car.
Oh, he did?
Yeah, he gave her a Pontiac or something like that.
I would have given her one, too, if I had been around. And she drove to New York, her and Valaida Snow. Valaida Snow was the girl trumpet.
She was a singer, too.
She was a performer. Oh, yeah, she was a performer. And I used to hang around with them.
You did a little more than hang around, Tom.
Oh, that's all. I'd hang around with them.
You're a good-looking guy and these were beautiful ladies.
